+## 🧽 Leave active producers before deleting storage
+
+**2026-11-04, accepted implementation choice; agent judgment under the owner's
+request to continue SPN-120. Native acceptance remains pending.**
+
+The catalog effect in `web/offline/useOfflineDownloads.ts` explicitly calls
+`prepareShell` for retained downloads. That reaches the worker's `prepare`
+command and `fillRuntime` in `web/offline/runtimeCache.ts`, whose `caches.open`
+can create the shell cache. The original trace does not identify which invocation
+recreated it; this is a concrete concurrent producer, not proof of an OS defect.
+[The service-worker lifecycle](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-service-workers-20261029/#unregister-algorithm)
+also explains why successful unregistration alone is insufficient: existing
+controlled clients and pending events can retain the worker.
+
+Choose a fixture-owned, same-origin inert document, with no scripts and a
+`default-src 'none'` policy. Navigate there after positively proving two available
+copies; this unloads the application's refresh/registration producers. Unregister
+workers there, retaining the still-present controller in evidence. Witness the
+existing adapter's graceful browser/driver exit, then reopen exactly that document
+through the existing `launch` function, which verifies the same profile and version.
+Only then delete storage, requiring the expected document, zero scripts, zero
+registered workers and no controller before the first storage mutation. The fresh
+document cannot start an application or worker. This is preparation, not a retry
+of deletion or of a failed postcondition.
+
+Keep one deletion request, the 28-second operation report inside the 30-second
+driver bound, the existing launch/stop bounds and 25-minute job bound. The separate
+unregistration request has the same 28-second bound and performs no cache/database
+deletion. Its failure prevents restart/deletion; stop/start failures remain fatal
+and flow through existing owned cleanup. Exactly one extra witnessed browser exit
+and same-profile start is expected per native owner. The final storage postconditions
+and all post-loss application assertions are unchanged. Other IndexedDB names remain
+diagnostics; only the private account database is targeted. No product path changes.
+
+Reject deletion from the active catalog, repeating cache deletion, fixed settling
+delays and broader timeouts. Navigation alone cannot prove that a pending worker
+event stopped; the owned restart supplies the additional lifecycle boundary.
+No general process or automation framework is added. Complete scope remains **L**:
+shared native fixture/lifecycle integration, negative controls and three-browser
+acceptance, with Safari's independent constructor defect still owned by SPN-140.
+
+Operator receives explicit preparation and deletion stages with first causes.
+Owner and Collaborator keep exact retained/reconnected/conflict content and honest
+missing-copy proof. Link guest access is unchanged. All four personas favor the
+strict absence check over accepting a cache that may still be populated.
+
+## 🔎 Concrete test plan and publication checkpoint

+`scripts/ci/desktop-storage.test.ts` owns deterministic serialized-script controls:
+the inert-document requirement, registration/controller rejection before mutation,
+unregistration without deletion, re-registration, successful deletion followed by
+cache recreation, blocked/retained databases, pending/rejected operations and a
+crashed driver with no diagnostic second request. First focused execution: **25/25
+passed**, 323 ms including watchdog, peak 92,560 KiB, normal memory pressure.
+It does not prove browser process lifetimes or native acceptance.
+
+The existing Desktop offline workflow owns that integration. Before publishing,
+declare **one first-attempt workflow triggered by this candidate's PR opening**:
+Chrome and Firefox on macOS 26, Safari on macOS 15 Intel, unchanged owners and
+25-minute bounds. Expect the original exact content/images/reconnect/conflict
+checks, inert preparation and unregistration, a fourth same-profile launch/exit,
+strict empty-storage proof and both post-loss assertions for every owner. Safari
+must also pass the unchanged capability sentinel/identity/baseline checks. Preserve
+any first failure; no unchanged rerun or automatic renewal is part of this plan.
+
+All changed runtime/test files are under `scripts/ci/desktop-*.ts`, already selected
+by the native workflow. Ordinary unknown script paths conservatively select full
+CI; no routing, assertion, retry or applicability change is needed. Full constrained
+typecheck and lint, backlog/index/PR validation and two independent committed-source
+grades precede publication. Hosted ordinary gates and selected native evidence
+remain pending until observed on the exact source/tested identities.
+
+Local constrained typecheck was **resource-aborted**, not passed: the watchdog

+## 🔎 Independent review repair: restored background clients
+
+Both nonimplementing reviewers rejected candidate
+`14147960accca0927f0b61dfd4c66b7de98685ec`: A **94/100** (35/20/19/10/10),
+B **92/100** (31/23/18/10/10). Their shared P2 finding was concrete: the existing
+Safari adapter permits restored background tabs, so checking the selected inert
+document alone does not establish producer quiescence. No validation push occurred.
+
+Repair the same acceptance gap here. The owned adapter inventories every window/tab
+(Safari) or WebDriver window handle (Chrome/Firefox). Before unregistration, navigate
+other tabs on this exact fixture origin to the inert URL once; leave unrelated
+origins unchanged. Retain before/after URL inventories. After the witnessed restart,
+inventory again in read-only mode and reject any fixture-origin URL other than the
+inert document; do not navigate a newly restored producer and proceed. WebDriver
+also rejects a changed handle set during inventory. Empty/malformed inventories
+and a missing inert tab fail. Existing PID/start identity is checked before native
+inventory; this adds no authority over a browser outside the owned adapter.
+
+Safari waits for the one navigation's observable URL result within two seconds,
+inside a five-second command bound; a pending navigation is never repeated. An
+inventory failure remains fatal and enters existing teardown. The inert page's
+script/worker/controller checks and strict storage deletion still follow this
+whole-browser boundary. No new product feature or broader framework is needed;
+scope remains L. Both reviewers must revalidate the repaired committed head.
+
+Added negative controls cover a background producer after restart, missing/empty
+inventories, unrelated origins, and navigation that never settles. The actual
+serialized Safari inventory script is exercised, including once-only mutation of
+the other fixture tab. **33/33 controls passed**, 300 ms including watchdog, peak
+91,328 KiB. Full lint/dependency/format checks passed in 16,916 ms at peak 766,704 KiB,
+with normal pressure throughout. These results supersede the pending tightened
+control/lint attempts above without erasing their resource dispositions. Hosted
+whole-browser process/native behavior remains explicitly pending.
+
+The repaired source's constrained full typecheck was also resource-aborted:
+pressure level 2 after 3,251 ms, peak observed 1,360,048 KiB. No TypeScript success
+is claimed and no diagnostic was emitted before termination. Hosted Typecheck
+owns the remaining check; do not repeatedly load this Mac under pressure.
+
+During revalidation of `cef07957450cfaddc23014c1533131371b656a3b`, reviewer A
+identified a second fixture weakness: WebDriver handle order is not stable.
+Compare validated unique handle membership rather than ordered arrays, retaining
+rejection of new/missing/duplicate/malformed handles. Add the reordered-same-set
+positive control and changed-set negatives before final committed-source review.
+The [WebDriver specification](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#get-window-handles)
+permits arbitrary order. A scored this source 96/100 (35/23/18/10/10) with that
+finding still open; B independently scored it 98/100 (35/25/18/10/10). Neither
+score authorized pushing with A's unresolved defect. After the repair, **34/34
+controls passed** in 301 ms at 91,360 KiB; formatting and changed-file lint passed.
+Both final reviews must identify the new committed source.

+The [Service Workers unregister and registration-clearing algorithms](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#unregister-algorithm)
+retain controlled clients after unregister and revisit clearing when the last
+client unloads or pending events settle. This motivates an explicit client-release
+boundary; it does not prove why the failed Safari run restored registration.
+The new choice supersedes immediate shutdown after unregistration above: once
+unregister succeeds, navigate every fixture-origin tab once to the inert route
+with a distinct query. A lost page-only marker proves a new document, and each
+tab must report complete loading, the inert marker, zero scripts and no controller.
+Account for all Safari window/tab positions or WebDriver handle membership;
+leave unrelated origins untouched. A same-document URL change cannot pass.
+Observe zero registrations and no controller once more before quitting, without
+deleting anything. Retain witnessed same-profile shutdown/restart and the unchanged
+strict post-restart storage precondition. A restored registration still fails
+before deletion. Null controllers do not independently prove every extended event
+finished, so the process and post-restart witnesses remain necessary.
+

metadata.gitDiff:
diff --git a/docs/implementation/SPN-141.md b/docs/implementation/SPN-141.md
index e1fddd8..0dc46cb 100644
--- a/docs/implementation/SPN-141.md
+++ b/docs/implementation/SPN-141.md
@@ -53,6 +53,351 @@ the post-loss assertions and every selected browser. Keep raw first failures and
 source/base/tested identities. Both independent exact-source grades precede push;
 mocks, unexecuted checks and retries cannot establish native acceptance.
 
+## 🧽 Leave active producers before deleting storage
+
+**2026-11-04, accepted implementation choice; agent judgment under the owner's
+request to continue SPN-120. Native acceptance remains pending.**
+
+The catalog effect in `web/offline/useOfflineDownloads.ts` explicitly calls
+`prepareShell` for retained downloads. That reaches the worker's `prepare`
+command and `fillRuntime` in `web/offline/runtimeCache.ts`, whose `caches.open`
+can create the shell cache. The original trace does not identify which invocation
+recreated it; this is a concrete concurrent producer, not proof of an OS defect.
+[The service-worker lifecycle](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-service-workers-20261029/#unregister-algorithm)
+also explains why successful unregistration alone is insufficient: existing
+controlled clients and pending events can retain the worker.
+
+Choose a fixture-owned, same-origin inert document, with no scripts and a
+`default-src 'none'` policy. Navigate there after positively proving two available
+copies; this unloads the application's refresh/registration producers. Unregister
+workers there, retaining the still-present controller in evidence. Witness the
+existing adapter's graceful browser/driver exit, then reopen exactly that document
+through the existing `launch` function, which verifies the same profile and version.
+Only then delete storage, requiring the expected document, zero scripts, zero
+registered workers and no controller before the first storage mutation. The fresh
+document cannot start an application or worker. This is preparation, not a retry
+of deletion or of a failed postcondition.
+
+Keep one deletion request, the 28-second operation report inside the 30-second
+driver bound, the existing launch/stop bounds and 25-minute job bound. The separate
+unregistration request has the same 28-second bound and performs no cache/database
+deletion. Its failure prevents restart/deletion; stop/start failures remain fatal
+and flow through existing owned cleanup. Exactly one extra witnessed browser exit
+and same-profile start is expected per native owner. The final storage postconditions
+and all post-loss application assertions are unchanged. Other IndexedDB names remain
+diagnostics; only the private account database is targeted. No product path changes.
+
+Reject deletion from the active catalog, repeating cache deletion, fixed settling
+delays and broader timeouts. Navigation alone cannot prove that a pending worker
+event stopped; the owned restart supplies the additional lifecycle boundary.
+No general process or automation framework is added. Complete scope remains **L**:
+shared native fixture/lifecycle integration, negative controls and three-browser
+acceptance, with Safari's independent constructor defect still owned by SPN-140.
+
+Operator receives explicit preparation and deletion stages with first causes.
+Owner and Collaborator keep exact retained/reconnected/conflict content and honest
+missing-copy proof. Link guest access is unchanged. All four personas favor the
+strict absence check over accepting a cache that may still be populated.
+
+## 🔎 Concrete test plan and publication checkpoint
+
+`scripts/ci/desktop-storage.test.ts` owns deterministic serialized-script controls:
+the inert-document requirement, registration/controller rejection before mutation,
+unregistration without deletion, re-registration, successful deletion followed by
+cache recreation, blocked/retained databases, pending/rejected operations and a
+crashed driver with no diagnostic second request. First focused execution: **25/25
+passed**, 323 ms including watchdog, peak 92,560 KiB, normal memory pressure.
+It does not prove browser process lifetimes or native acceptance.
+
+The existing Desktop offline workflow owns that integration. Before publishing,
+declare **one first-attempt workflow triggered by this candidate's PR opening**:
+Chrome and Firefox on macOS 26, Safari on macOS 15 Intel, unchanged owners and
+25-minute bounds. Expect the original exact content/images/reconnect/conflict
+checks, inert preparation and unregistration, a fourth same-profile launch/exit,
+strict empty-storage proof and both post-loss assertions for every owner. Safari
+must also pass the unchanged capability sentinel/identity/baseline checks. Preserve
+any first failure; no unchanged rerun or automatic renewal is part of this plan.
+
+All changed runtime/test files are under `scripts/ci/desktop-*.ts`, already selected
+by the native workflow. Ordinary unknown script paths conservatively select full
+CI; no routing, assertion, retry or applicability change is needed. Full constrained
+typecheck and lint, backlog/index/PR validation and two independent committed-source
+grades precede publication. Hosted ordinary gates and selected native evidence
+remain pending until observed on the exact source/tested identities.
+
+Local constrained typecheck was **resource-aborted**, not passed: the watchdog
+observed macOS pressure level 2 after 1,706 ms at 1,296,288 KiB. Subsequent
+format/focused-control/lint launches were refused at pressure 2. The first 25-test
+pass predates only a tighter asynchronous cache-recreation control and formatting;
+that refinement requires a fresh run when pressure is normal. Retain both results.
+
+## 🏁 Prepared landing bookkeeping
+
+Delete SPN-141's ticket, remove its dependency from SPN-120, append its completion
+counter and regenerate the index in this candidate. These are prepared landing
+changes; they do not declare pending native acceptance complete. SPN-140 and
+SPN-120 retain their own full obligations. Final run identities, measured results,
+both exact-source reviews and failure dispositions belong in the PR description
+or immutable maintained evidence before obsolete branches are removed.
+
+## 🔎 Independent review repair: restored background clients
+
+Both nonimplementing reviewers rejected candidate
+`14147960accca0927f0b61dfd4c66b7de98685ec`: A **94/100** (35/20/19/10/10),
+B **92/100** (31/23/18/10/10). Their shared P2 finding was concrete: the existing
+Safari adapter permits restored background tabs, so checking the selected inert
+document alone does not establish producer quiescence. No validation push occurred.
+
+Repair the same acceptance gap here. The owned adapter inventories every window/tab
+(Safari) or WebDriver window handle (Chrome/Firefox). Before unregistration, navigate
+other tabs on this exact fixture origin to the inert URL once; leave unrelated
+origins unchanged. Retain before/after URL inventories. After the witnessed restart,
+inventory again in read-only mode and reject any fixture-origin URL other than the
+inert document; do not navigate a newly restored producer and proceed. WebDriver
+also rejects a changed handle set during inventory. Empty/malformed inventories
+and a missing inert tab fail. Existing PID/start identity is checked before native
+inventory; this adds no authority over a browser outside the owned adapter.
+
+Safari waits for the one navigation's observable URL result within two seconds,
+inside a five-second command bound; a pending navigation is never repeated. An
+inventory failure remains fatal and enters existing teardown. The inert page's
+script/worker/controller checks and strict storage deletion still follow this
+whole-browser boundary. No new product feature or broader framework is needed;
+scope remains L. Both reviewers must revalidate the repaired committed head.
+
+Added negative controls cover a background producer after restart, missing/empty
+inventories, unrelated origins, and navigation that never settles. The actual
+serialized Safari inventory script is exercised, including once-only mutation of
+the other fixture tab. **33/33 controls passed**, 300 ms including watchdog, peak
+91,328 KiB. Full lint/dependency/format checks passed in 16,916 ms at peak 766,704 KiB,
+with normal pressure throughout. These results supersede the pending tightened
+control/lint attempts above without erasing their resource dispositions. Hosted
+whole-browser process/native behavior remains explicitly pending.
+
+The repaired source's constrained full typecheck was also resource-aborted:
+pressure level 2 after 3,251 ms, peak observed 1,360,048 KiB. No TypeScript success
+is claimed and no diagnostic was emitted before termination. Hosted Typecheck
+owns the remaining check; do not repeatedly load this Mac under pressure.
+
+During revalidation of `cef07957450cfaddc23014c1533131371b656a3b`, reviewer A
+identified a second fixture weakness: WebDriver handle order is not stable.
+Compare validated unique handle membership rather than ordered arrays, retaining
+rejection of new/missing/duplicate/malformed handles. Add the reordered-same-set
+positive control and changed-set negatives before final committed-source review.
+The [WebDriver specification](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#get-window-handles)
+permits arbitrary order. A scored this source 96/100 (35/23/18/10/10) with that
+finding still open; B independently scored it 98/100 (35/25/18/10/10). Neither
+score authorized pushing with A's unresolved defect. After the repair, **34/34
+controls passed** in 301 ms at 91,360 KiB; formatting and changed-file lint passed.
+Both final reviews must identify the new committed source.
+
+## 📦 First hosted source and prerequisite integration
+
+2026-11-04 — candidate `2f1c9304b15adfef833e53f12c4facff9ce14821`
+received independent pre-push grades A99/100 (35/25/19/10/10) and B98/100
+(35/25/18/10/10), with both findings above resolved. Tested merge
+`a554c611c96556176bcc6b2ba006ea421ee00943` and source share tree
+`faac771987098438ff4f9269ef27d20a1a2bb7e2` on main
+`5d8676ec280ac6d5cc9dcedb7e9cc09527b24806`. Agent review only.
+
+Native run41885019409 attempt1 passed Chrome job126767084103 and Safari
+job126767084191. Independent reviews accept each owner's same-profile lifecycle,
+original/pending content and image retention, exact reconnect, conflict copies,
+whole-browser inert inventories, uncontrolled deletion, empty storage witnesses
+and post-loss unavailable state. These actual runs each had one tab; deterministic
+controls own the background-tab negatives. Safari's earlier constructor failure
+is not erased, and SPN-140 remains separately required.
+
+Firefox job126767083588 never acquired a runner. Its zero runner ID, empty steps
+and hosted ARM64 capacity annotations support an infrastructure disposition,
+not a browser failure. A separately reviewed one-job provisioning allowance was
+[preserved before execution](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/tree/2bf0b3adba598239a953f87ae20ca485646f2fad/docs/review-assets/spn-141-native-2f1c9304/provisioning).
+Attempt2/job126779992912 also ended without a runner or any steps. Chrome/Safari
+entries carried into attempt2 retain their original execution timestamps; they
+were not run again. The allowance is exhausted; no further unchanged provisioning
+retry is declared. No Firefox scenario acceptance is claimed.
+
+📦 [Immutable native reports, images, logs, source reviews and both capacity failures](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/tree/9c34b3796ce761513edb7d1e063d1556ca8d35d5/docs/review-assets/spn-141-native-2f1c9304)
+preserve this partial checkpoint. Ordinary CI41885019303 passed all selected
+workers except historical mobile callback comparison job126767285654; the
+Playwright aggregate correctly failed. Storybook41885019510 passed. Hosted
+Typecheck passed, resolving the local resource limitation for that source.
+
+The callback baseline timed out after420000ms while candidate passed. Its valid
+retained trace reaches the final key, disposal and end; the persisted typing phase
+is stale and the exact interrupted collection operation remains unknown.
+[Immutable first failure and independent diagnosis](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/tree/46a99b8c1786cb9f80695689c70077ce3ef7cf5d/docs/review-assets/spn-134-recurrence-2f1c9304)
+assign the existing diagnostic defect to SPN-134 / PR #248. Its later success
+cannot retroactively pass this source. Integrate its accepted squash before
+SPN-141's next validation; preserve this native repair's separate ownership.
+
+Prospective integration protocol: after the accepted SPN-134 base update, run
+relevant local checks, complete bookkeeping and obtain both qualifying reviews
+on the exact new commit. One normal synchronization of PR #258 then owns all
+selected checks and a fresh first-attempt native workflow with the unchanged
+Chrome/Safari/Firefox runner matrix, budgets and complete application assertions.
+This is required validation of the integrated source, not credit from old green
+jobs. The hypothesis remains producer quiescence before one strict deletion;
+SPN-134 changes failure attribution, not storage behavior or runner capacity.
+No additional unchanged scenario/provisioning retry is included. If capacity
+again prevents execution, keep that owner unavailable and inspect the result.
+Do not publish this integrated candidate before its prerequisite is accepted.
+
+The accepted SPN-134 squash is now
+`13b74ecea5f2552627ff638be9413ad4754ef581` ([PR #248](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/pull/248)).
+Its source `97b0db550385b51cdbc8f0543aaa21524c1e05dc` passed all33 selected
+ordinary jobs, seven required gates, Storybook and both independently reviewed
+first-attempt callback pairs. [Immutable acceptance](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/tree/8e85622a42b9b936cef1e3b21e1ca044d2bebb03/docs/review-assets/spn-134-acceptance-97b0db55)
+retains its exact identities and historical uncertainty. Integrating that squash
+preserves the SPN-141 storage implementation and incorporates the diagnostic
+repair through main. New-source native and ordinary checks remain pending under
+the one-synchronization protocol above; no prior run is substituted for them.
+
+✅ [Integrated local evidence and five source hashes](evidence/SPN-141-integration.json):
+34 storage/inventory controls pass (310 ms watchdog elapsed, 90592 KiB sampled
+peak); full lint/dependency/format passes (16810 ms, 734256 KiB); focused types
+cover all five changed TypeScript roots and imports (1453 ms, 643968 KiB).
+All ran with normal memory pressure. Full-project types and current-source native
+acceptance remain hosted obligations. Backlog, generated index, PR title/shape
+and whitespace checks pass. Both reviewers must grade this complete committed
+integration before publication.
+
+## 🧭 Release controlled clients before shutdown
+
+**2026-11-04, in-scope repair after actual integrated Safari failure; agent
+judgment under the owner's continued SPN-120 merge request. Native proof pending.**
+
+Integrated source `388262cc619f6caa162bc71881f22a714d0ddf69`, base
+`13b74ecea5f2552627ff638be9413ad4754ef581`, tested merge
+`b684654080d4f22cc1cf8d03e56cc523f4df3d57`, shared tree
+`179b7a51a4dd021dd62a42847c91b9575d76eb1a` received both independent 98/100
+pre-push grades. Native run41900102794 attempt1 passed Chrome126819901056 and
+Firefox126819901624, with independent complete-flow audits. This was Firefox's
+first actual execution; previous capacity failures remain unexecuted.
+
+Safari126819901608 passed capability, offline content/images, edits, reconnect
+and conflict-copy stages, then failed before any cache/localStorage/database
+mutation. At19:56:26.476Z unregister had returned true and registrations were
+empty, while the inert document still had a controller. PID7804 exited; the same
+profile restarted as PID11512. At19:56:34.873Z strict verification found the root
+registration and controller again. The final process exit was witnessed. This is
+not SPN-140's constructor failure; the Safari persistence mechanism is unproven.
+
+📦 [Immutable first failure, all native reports/images/logs and independent reviews](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/tree/f8e24b41b73eb9d4414597aba2c3396a931a9408/docs/review-assets/spn-141-native-388262cc)
+preserve artifact13359075911, ZIP SHA-256
+`0c0148ac6d286b3d5f5c01c55ff152054c6f61f458d5f557f125a05107e0b318`.
+Ordinary CI41900102989 and Storybook41900102783 were incomplete snapshots in
+that first archive. Their terminal attempt1 receipts are now preserved in
+[the later integration evidence](evidence/SPN-141-after143/README.md): CI was
+completed/cancelled and Storybook completed/success on exact388262cc. Ten CI
+workers and the browser aggregate were cancelled; Unit aggregate126833489868
+failed closed with `Incomplete coverage unit-tests: selected=true, result=cancelled`.
+That failed aggregate represents a cancelled selected worker, not a retained
+unit assertion failure; the raw aggregate log confirms the cause. This source
+never completed ordinary acceptance and receives no current-source credit.
+No old native pass validates this repair.
+
+The [Service Workers unregister and registration-clearing algorithms](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#unregister-algorithm)
+retain controlled clients after unregister and revisit clearing when the last
+client unloads or pending events settle. This motivates an explicit client-release
+boundary; it does not prove why the failed Safari run restored registration.
+The new choice supersedes immediate shutdown after unregistration above: once
+unregister succeeds, navigate every fixture-origin tab once to the inert route
+with a distinct query. A lost page-only marker proves a new document, and each
+tab must report complete loading, the inert marker, zero scripts and no controller.
+Account for all Safari window/tab positions or WebDriver handle membership;
+leave unrelated origins untouched. A same-document URL change cannot pass.
+Observe zero registrations and no controller once more before quitting, without
+deleting anything. Retain witnessed same-profile shutdown/restart and the unchanged
+strict post-restart storage precondition. A restored registration still fails
+before deletion. Null controllers do not independently prove every extended event
+finished, so the process and post-restart witnesses remain necessary.
+
+Reject another unregister, another deletion, fixed sleeps, deadline extensions
+and unchanged-source reruns. Safari retains its existing 2-second inventory
+observation within one 5-second native request; failed native requests propagate
+immediately. Each new browser observation uses the existing 28/30-second bound.
+No product behavior, routing exclusion, runner matrix or job budget changes.
+The complete outcome remains L: native lifecycle acceptance is retained here;
+SPN-140 constructor work and SPN-120's finite audit retain their separate scope.
+
+Operator gains evidence that the old controlled clients were actually released.
+Owner and Collaborator keep exact persisted-content and recovery assertions.
+Link guest access is unchanged; synthetic fixture isolation keeps this preparation
+away from user documents. All four favor observable release over guessing a delay.
+
+🧪 [Handoff local evidence, first failed fixture control and source hashes](evidence/SPN-141-handoff.json)
+records 46 passing actual serialized controls, full lint/dependency/format and
+focused types for all five changed roots/imports. The first controlled-client
+negative used an invalid mock controller without scriptURL; correcting the mock
+preserves the real controller contract. An initial compiler command named a
+nonexistent package; the corrected repository compiler passed. Neither failed
+attempt is omitted. Full hosted types/native acceptance remain pending.
+
+After complete-candidate commit and two new independent qualifying reviews,
+declare one repair synchronization of PR #258: all selected ordinary checks and
+one first-attempt Chrome/Safari/Firefox native workflow, unchanged assertions and
+budgets. Hypothesis: releasing every controlled client before normal shutdown
+establishes the missing lifecycle boundary. No further unchanged scenario or
+provisioning retry is included. Preserve any new first failure and assess it.
+
+## 🔗 Integrate accepted capacity and trace prerequisites

metadata.gitDiff:
diff --git a/docs/implementation/SPN-141.md b/docs/implementation/SPN-141.md
index e1fddd8..0dc46cb 100644
--- a/docs/implementation/SPN-141.md
+++ b/docs/implementation/SPN-141.md
@@ -53,6 +53,351 @@ the post-loss assertions and every selected browser. Keep raw first failures and
 source/base/tested identities. Both independent exact-source grades precede push;
 mocks, unexecuted checks and retries cannot establish native acceptance.
 
+## 🧽 Leave active producers before deleting storage
+
+**2026-11-04, accepted implementation choice; agent judgment under the owner's
+request to continue SPN-120. Native acceptance remains pending.**
+
+The catalog effect in `web/offline/useOfflineDownloads.ts` explicitly calls
+`prepareShell` for retained downloads. That reaches the worker's `prepare`
+command and `fillRuntime` in `web/offline/runtimeCache.ts`, whose `caches.open`
+can create the shell cache. The original trace does not identify which invocation
+recreated it; this is a concrete concurrent producer, not proof of an OS defect.
+[The service-worker lifecycle](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-service-workers-20261029/#unregister-algorithm)
+also explains why successful unregistration alone is insufficient: existing
+controlled clients and pending events can retain the worker.
+
+Choose a fixture-owned, same-origin inert document, with no scripts and a
+`default-src 'none'` policy. Navigate there after positively proving two available
+copies; this unloads the application's refresh/registration producers. Unregister
+workers there, retaining the still-present controller in evidence. Witness the
+existing adapter's graceful browser/driver exit, then reopen exactly that document
+through the existing `launch` function, which verifies the same profile and version.
+Only then delete storage, requiring the expected document, zero scripts, zero
+registered workers and no controller before the first storage mutation. The fresh
+document cannot start an application or worker. This is preparation, not a retry
+of deletion or of a failed postcondition.
+
+Keep one deletion request, the 28-second operation report inside the 30-second
+driver bound, the existing launch/stop bounds and 25-minute job bound. The separate
+unregistration request has the same 28-second bound and performs no cache/database
+deletion. Its failure prevents restart/deletion; stop/start failures remain fatal
+and flow through existing owned cleanup. Exactly one extra witnessed browser exit
+and same-profile start is expected per native owner. The final storage postconditions
+and all post-loss application assertions are unchanged. Other IndexedDB names remain
+diagnostics; only the private account database is targeted. No product path changes.
+
+Reject deletion from the active catalog, repeating cache deletion, fixed settling
+delays and broader timeouts. Navigation alone cannot prove that a pending worker
+event stopped; the owned restart supplies the additional lifecycle boundary.
+No general process or automation framework is added. Complete scope remains **L**:
+shared native fixture/lifecycle integration, negative controls and three-browser
+acceptance, with Safari's independent constructor defect still owned by SPN-140.
+
+Operator receives explicit preparation and deletion stages with first causes.
+Owner and Collaborator keep exact retained/reconnected/conflict content and honest
+missing-copy proof. Link guest access is unchanged. All four personas favor the
+strict absence check over accepting a cache that may still be populated.
+
+## 🔎 Concrete test plan and publication checkpoint
+
+`scripts/ci/desktop-storage.test.ts` owns deterministic serialized-script controls:
+the inert-document requirement, registration/controller rejection before mutation,
+unregistration without deletion, re-registration, successful deletion followed by
+cache recreation, blocked/retained databases, pending/rejected operations and a
+crashed driver with no diagnostic second request. First focused execution: **25/25
+passed**, 323 ms including watchdog, peak 92,560 KiB, normal memory pressure.
+It does not prove browser process lifetimes or native acceptance.
+
+The existing Desktop offline workflow owns that integration. Before publishing,
+declare **one first-attempt workflow triggered by this candidate's PR opening**:
+Chrome and Firefox on macOS 26, Safari on macOS 15 Intel, unchanged owners and
+25-minute bounds. Expect the original exact content/images/reconnect/conflict
+checks, inert preparation and unregistration, a fourth same-profile launch/exit,
+strict empty-storage proof and both post-loss assertions for every owner. Safari
+must also pass the unchanged capability sentinel/identity/baseline checks. Preserve
+any first failure; no unchanged rerun or automatic renewal is part of this plan.
+
+All changed runtime/test files are under `scripts/ci/desktop-*.ts`, already selected
+by the native workflow. Ordinary unknown script paths conservatively select full
+CI; no routing, assertion, retry or applicability change is needed. Full constrained
+typecheck and lint, backlog/index/PR validation and two independent committed-source
+grades precede publication. Hosted ordinary gates and selected native evidence
+remain pending until observed on the exact source/tested identities.
+
+Local constrained typecheck was **resource-aborted**, not passed: the watchdog
+observed macOS pressure level 2 after 1,706 ms at 1,296,288 KiB. Subsequent
+format/focused-control/lint launches were refused at pressure 2. The first 25-test
+pass predates only a tighter asynchronous cache-recreation control and formatting;
+that refinement requires a fresh run when pressure is normal. Retain both results.
+
+## 🏁 Prepared landing bookkeeping
+
+Delete SPN-141's ticket, remove its dependency from SPN-120, append its completion
+counter and regenerate the index in this candidate. These are prepared landing
+changes; they do not declare pending native acceptance complete. SPN-140 and
+SPN-120 retain their own full obligations. Final run identities, measured results,
+both exact-source reviews and failure dispositions belong in the PR description
+or immutable maintained evidence before obsolete branches are removed.
+
+## 🔎 Independent review repair: restored background clients
+
+Both nonimplementing reviewers rejected candidate
+`14147960accca0927f0b61dfd4c66b7de98685ec`: A **94/100** (35/20/19/10/10),
+B **92/100** (31/23/18/10/10). Their shared P2 finding was concrete: the existing
+Safari adapter permits restored background tabs, so checking the selected inert
+document alone does not establish producer quiescence. No validation push occurred.
+
+Repair the same acceptance gap here. The owned adapter inventories every window/tab
+(Safari) or WebDriver window handle (Chrome/Firefox). Before unregistration, navigate
+other tabs on this exact fixture origin to the inert URL once; leave unrelated
+origins unchanged. Retain before/after URL inventories. After the witnessed restart,
+inventory again in read-only mode and reject any fixture-origin URL other than the
+inert document; do not navigate a newly restored producer and proceed. WebDriver
+also rejects a changed handle set during inventory. Empty/malformed inventories
+and a missing inert tab fail. Existing PID/start identity is checked before native
+inventory; this adds no authority over a browser outside the owned adapter.
+
+Safari waits for the one navigation's observable URL result within two seconds,
+inside a five-second command bound; a pending navigation is never repeated. An
+inventory failure remains fatal and enters existing teardown. The inert page's
+script/worker/controller checks and strict storage deletion still follow this
+whole-browser boundary. No new product feature or broader framework is needed;
+scope remains L. Both reviewers must revalidate the repaired committed head.
+
+Added negative controls cover a background producer after restart, missing/empty
+inventories, unrelated origins, and navigation that never settles. The actual
+serialized Safari inventory script is exercised, including once-only mutation of
+the other fixture tab. **33/33 controls passed**, 300 ms including watchdog, peak
+91,328 KiB. Full lint/dependency/format checks passed in 16,916 ms at peak 766,704 KiB,
+with normal pressure throughout. These results supersede the pending tightened
+control/lint attempts above without erasing their resource dispositions. Hosted
+whole-browser process/native behavior remains explicitly pending.
+
+The repaired source's constrained full typecheck was also resource-aborted:
+pressure level 2 after 3,251 ms, peak observed 1,360,048 KiB. No TypeScript success
+is claimed and no diagnostic was emitted before termination. Hosted Typecheck
+owns the remaining check; do not repeatedly load this Mac under pressure.
+
+During revalidation of `cef07957450cfaddc23014c1533131371b656a3b`, reviewer A
+identified a second fixture weakness: WebDriver handle order is not stable.
+Compare validated unique handle membership rather than ordered arrays, retaining
+rejection of new/missing/duplicate/malformed handles. Add the reordered-same-set
+positive control and changed-set negatives before final committed-source review.
+The [WebDriver specification](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#get-window-handles)
+permits arbitrary order. A scored this source 96/100 (35/23/18/10/10) with that
+finding still open; B independently scored it 98/100 (35/25/18/10/10). Neither
+score authorized pushing with A's unresolved defect. After the repair, **34/34
+controls passed** in 301 ms at 91,360 KiB; formatting and changed-file lint passed.
+Both final reviews must identify the new committed source.
+
+## 📦 First hosted source and prerequisite integration
+
+2026-11-04 — candidate `2f1c9304b15adfef833e53f12c4facff9ce14821`
+received independent pre-push grades A99/100 (35/25/19/10/10) and B98/100
+(35/25/18/10/10), with both findings above resolved. Tested merge
+`a554c611c96556176bcc6b2ba006ea421ee00943` and source share tree
+`faac771987098438ff4f9269ef27d20a1a2bb7e2` on main
+`5d8676ec280ac6d5cc9dcedb7e9cc09527b24806`. Agent review only.
+
+Native run41885019409 attempt1 passed Chrome job126767084103 and Safari
+job126767084191. Independent reviews accept each owner's same-profile lifecycle,
+original/pending content and image retention, exact reconnect, conflict copies,
+whole-browser inert inventories, uncontrolled deletion, empty storage witnesses
+and post-loss unavailable state. These actual runs each had one tab; deterministic
+controls own the background-tab negatives. Safari's earlier constructor failure
+is not erased, and SPN-140 remains separately required.
+
+Firefox job126767083588 never acquired a runner. Its zero runner ID, empty steps

@@ -53,6 +53,351 @@ the post-loss assertions and every selected browser. Keep raw first failures and
 source/base/tested identities. Both independent exact-source grades precede push;
 mocks, unexecuted checks and retries cannot establish native acceptance.
 
+## 🧽 Leave active producers before deleting storage
+
+**2026-11-04, accepted implementation choice; agent judgment under the owner's
+request to continue SPN-120. Native acceptance remains pending.**
+
+The catalog effect in `web/offline/useOfflineDownloads.ts` explicitly calls
+`prepareShell` for retained downloads. That reaches the worker's `prepare`
+command and `fillRuntime` in `web/offline/runtimeCache.ts`, whose `caches.open`
+can create the shell cache. The original trace does not identify which invocation
+recreated it; this is a concrete concurrent producer, not proof of an OS defect.
+[The service-worker lifecycle](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-service-workers-20261029/#unregister-algorithm)
+also explains why successful unregistration alone is insufficient: existing
+controlled clients and pending events can retain the worker.
+
+Choose a fixture-owned, same-origin inert document, with no scripts and a
+`default-src 'none'` policy. Navigate there after positively proving two available
+copies; this unloads the application's refresh/registration producers. Unregister
+workers there, retaining the still-present controller in evidence. Witness the
+existing adapter's graceful browser/driver exit, then reopen exactly that document
+through the existing `launch` function, which verifies the same profile and version.
+Only then delete storage, requiring the expected document, zero scripts, zero
+registered workers and no controller before the first storage mutation. The fresh
+document cannot start an application or worker. This is preparation, not a retry
+of deletion or of a failed postcondition.
+
+Keep one deletion request, the 28-second operation report inside the 30-second
+driver bound, the existing launch/stop bounds and 25-minute job bound. The separate
+unregistration request has the same 28-second bound and performs no cache/database
+deletion. Its failure prevents restart/deletion; stop/start failures remain fatal
+and flow through existing owned cleanup. Exactly one extra witnessed browser exit
+and same-profile start is expected per native owner. The final storage postconditions
+and all post-loss application assertions are unchanged. Other IndexedDB names remain
+diagnostics; only the private account database is targeted. No product path changes.
+
+Reject deletion from the active catalog, repeating cache deletion, fixed settling
+delays and broader timeouts. Navigation alone cannot prove that a pending worker
+event stopped; the owned restart supplies the additional lifecycle boundary.
+No general process or automation framework is added. Complete scope remains **L**:
+shared native fixture/lifecycle integration, negative controls and three-browser
+acceptance, with Safari's independent constructor defect still owned by SPN-140.
+
+Operator receives explicit preparation and deletion stages with first causes.
+Owner and Collaborator keep exact retained/reconnected/conflict content and honest
+missing-copy proof. Link guest access is unchanged. All four personas favor the
+strict absence check over accepting a cache that may still be populated.
+
+## 🔎 Concrete test plan and publication checkpoint
+
+`scripts/ci/desktop-storage.test.ts` owns deterministic serialized-script controls:
+the inert-document requirement, registration/controller rejection before mutation,
+unregistration without deletion, re-registration, successful deletion followed by
+cache recreation, blocked/retained databases, pending/rejected operations and a
+crashed driver with no diagnostic second request. First focused execution: **25/25
+passed**, 323 ms including watchdog, peak 92,560 KiB, normal memory pressure.
+It does not prove browser process lifetimes or native acceptance.
+
+The existing Desktop offline workflow owns that integration. Before publishing,
+declare **one first-attempt workflow triggered by this candidate's PR opening**:
+Chrome and Firefox on macOS 26, Safari on macOS 15 Intel, unchanged owners and
+25-minute bounds. Expect the original exact content/images/reconnect/conflict
+checks, inert preparation and unregistration, a fourth same-profile launch/exit,
+strict empty-storage proof and both post-loss assertions for every owner. Safari
+must also pass the unchanged capability sentinel/identity/baseline checks. Preserve
+any first failure; no unchanged rerun or automatic renewal is part of this plan.
+
+All changed runtime/test files are under `scripts/ci/desktop-*.ts`, already selected
+by the native workflow. Ordinary unknown script paths conservatively select full
+CI; no routing, assertion, retry or applicability change is needed. Full constrained
+typecheck and lint, backlog/index/PR validation and two independent committed-source
+grades precede publication. Hosted ordinary gates and selected native evidence
+remain pending until observed on the exact source/tested identities.
+
+Local constrained typecheck was **resource-aborted**, not passed: the watchdog
+observed macOS pressure level 2 after 1,706 ms at 1,296,288 KiB. Subsequent
+format/focused-control/lint launches were refused at pressure 2. The first 25-test
+pass predates only a tighter asynchronous cache-recreation control and formatting;
+that refinement requires a fresh run when pressure is normal. Retain both results.
+
+## 🏁 Prepared landing bookkeeping
+
+Delete SPN-141's ticket, remove its dependency from SPN-120, append its completion
+counter and regenerate the index in this candidate. These are prepared landing
+changes; they do not declare pending native acceptance complete. SPN-140 and
+SPN-120 retain their own full obligations. Final run identities, measured results,
+both exact-source reviews and failure dispositions belong in the PR description
+or immutable maintained evidence before obsolete branches are removed.
+
+## 🔎 Independent review repair: restored background clients
+
+Both nonimplementing reviewers rejected candidate
+`14147960accca0927f0b61dfd4c66b7de98685ec`: A **94/100** (35/20/19/10/10),
+B **92/100** (31/23/18/10/10). Their shared P2 finding was concrete: the existing
+Safari adapter permits restored background tabs, so checking the selected inert
+document alone does not establish producer quiescence. No validation push occurred.
+
+Repair the same acceptance gap here. The owned adapter inventories every window/tab
+(Safari) or WebDriver window handle (Chrome/Firefox). Before unregistration, navigate
+other tabs on this exact fixture origin to the inert URL once; leave unrelated
+origins unchanged. Retain before/after URL inventories. After the witnessed restart,
+inventory again in read-only mode and reject any fixture-origin URL other than the
+inert document; do not navigate a newly restored producer and proceed. WebDriver
+also rejects a changed handle set during inventory. Empty/malformed inventories
+and a missing inert tab fail. Existing PID/start identity is checked before native
+inventory; this adds no authority over a browser outside the owned adapter.
+
+Safari waits for the one navigation's observable URL result within two seconds,
+inside a five-second command bound; a pending navigation is never repeated. An
+inventory failure remains fatal and enters existing teardown. The inert page's
+script/worker/controller checks and strict storage deletion still follow this
+whole-browser boundary. No new product feature or broader framework is needed;
+scope remains L. Both reviewers must revalidate the repaired committed head.
+
+Added negative controls cover a background producer after restart, missing/empty
+inventories, unrelated origins, and navigation that never settles. The actual
+serialized Safari inventory script is exercised, including once-only mutation of
+the other fixture tab. **33/33 controls passed**, 300 ms including watchdog, peak
+91,328 KiB. Full lint/dependency/format checks passed in 16,916 ms at peak 766,704 KiB,
+with normal pressure throughout. These results supersede the pending tightened
+control/lint attempts above without erasing their resource dispositions. Hosted
+whole-browser process/native behavior remains explicitly pending.
+
+The repaired source's constrained full typecheck was also resource-aborted:
+pressure level 2 after 3,251 ms, peak observed 1,360,048 KiB. No TypeScript success
+is claimed and no diagnostic was emitted before termination. Hosted Typecheck
+owns the remaining check; do not repeatedly load this Mac under pressure.
+
+During revalidation of `cef07957450cfaddc23014c1533131371b656a3b`, reviewer A
+identified a second fixture weakness: WebDriver handle order is not stable.
+Compare validated unique handle membership rather than ordered arrays, retaining
+rejection of new/missing/duplicate/malformed handles. Add the reordered-same-set
+positive control and changed-set negatives before final committed-source review.
+The [WebDriver specification](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#get-window-handles)
+permits arbitrary order. A scored this source 96/100 (35/23/18/10/10) with that
+finding still open; B independently scored it 98/100 (35/25/18/10/10). Neither
+score authorized pushing with A's unresolved defect. After the repair, **34/34
+controls passed** in 301 ms at 91,360 KiB; formatting and changed-file lint passed.
+Both final reviews must identify the new committed source.
+
+## 📦 First hosted source and prerequisite integration
+
+2026-11-04 — candidate `2f1c9304b15adfef833e53f12c4facff9ce14821`
+received independent pre-push grades A99/100 (35/25/19/10/10) and B98/100
+(35/25/18/10/10), with both findings above resolved. Tested merge
+`a554c611c96556176bcc6b2ba006ea421ee00943` and source share tree
+`faac771987098438ff4f9269ef27d20a1a2bb7e2` on main
+`5d8676ec280ac6d5cc9dcedb7e9cc09527b24806`. Agent review only.
+
+Native run41885019409 attempt1 passed Chrome job126767084103 and Safari
+job126767084191. Independent reviews accept each owner's same-profile lifecycle,
+original/pending content and image retention, exact reconnect, conflict copies,
+whole-browser inert inventories, uncontrolled deletion, empty storage witnesses
+and post-loss unavailable state. These actual runs each had one tab; deterministic
+controls own the background-tab negatives. Safari's earlier constructor failure
+is not erased, and SPN-140 remains separately required.
+
+Firefox job126767083588 never acquired a runner. Its zero runner ID, empty steps
+and hosted ARM64 capacity annotations support an infrastructure disposition,
+not a browser failure. A separately reviewed one-job provisioning allowance was
+[preserved before execution](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/tree/2bf0b3adba598239a953f87ae20ca485646f2fad/docs/review-assets/spn-141-native-2f1c9304/provisioning).
+Attempt2/job126779992912 also ended without a runner or any steps. Chrome/Safari
+entries carried into attempt2 retain their original execution timestamps; they
+were not run again. The allowance is exhausted; no further unchanged provisioning
+retry is declared. No Firefox scenario acceptance is claimed.
+
+📦 [Immutable native reports, images, logs, source reviews and both capacity failures](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/tree/9c34b3796ce761513edb7d1e063d1556ca8d35d5/docs/review-assets/spn-141-native-2f1c9304)
+preserve this partial checkpoint. Ordinary CI41885019303 passed all selected
+workers except historical mobile callback comparison job126767285654; the
+Playwright aggregate correctly failed. Storybook41885019510 passed. Hosted
+Typecheck passed, resolving the local resource limitation for that source.
+
+The callback baseline timed out after420000ms while candidate passed. Its valid
+retained trace reaches the final key, disposal and end; the persisted typing phase
+is stale and the exact interrupted collection operation remains unknown.
+[Immutable first failure and independent diagnosis](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/tree/46a99b8c1786cb9f80695689c70077ce3ef7cf5d/docs/review-assets/spn-134-recurrence-2f1c9304)
+assign the existing diagnostic defect to SPN-134 / PR #248. Its later success
+cannot retroactively pass this source. Integrate its accepted squash before
+SPN-141's next validation; preserve this native repair's separate ownership.
+
+Prospective integration protocol: after the accepted SPN-134 base update, run
+relevant local checks, complete bookkeeping and obtain both qualifying reviews
+on the exact new commit. One normal synchronization of PR #258 then owns all
+selected checks and a fresh first-attempt native workflow with the unchanged
+Chrome/Safari/Firefox runner matrix, budgets and complete application assertions.
+This is required validation of the integrated source, not credit from old green
+jobs. The hypothesis remains producer quiescence before one strict deletion;
+SPN-134 changes failure attribution, not storage behavior or runner capacity.
+No additional unchanged scenario/provisioning retry is included. If capacity
+again prevents execution, keep that owner unavailable and inspect the result.
+Do not publish this integrated candidate before its prerequisite is accepted.
+
+The accepted SPN-134 squash is now
+`13b74ecea5f2552627ff638be9413ad4754ef581` ([PR #248](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/pull/248)).
+Its source `97b0db550385b51cdbc8f0543aaa21524c1e05dc` passed all33 selected
+ordinary jobs, seven required gates, Storybook and both independently reviewed
+first-attempt callback pairs. [Immutable acceptance](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/tree/8e85622a42b9b936cef1e3b21e1ca044d2bebb03/docs/review-assets/spn-134-acceptance-97b0db55)
+retains its exact identities and historical uncertainty. Integrating that squash

+
+✅ [Integrated local evidence and five source hashes](evidence/SPN-141-integration.json):
+34 storage/inventory controls pass (310 ms watchdog elapsed, 90592 KiB sampled
+peak); full lint/dependency/format passes (16810 ms, 734256 KiB); focused types

+
+## 🧭 Release controlled clients before shutdown
+
+**2026-11-04, in-scope repair after actual integrated Safari failure; agent
+judgment under the owner's continued SPN-120 merge request. Native proof pending.**
+
+Integrated source `388262cc619f6caa162bc71881f22a714d0ddf69`, base
+`13b74ecea5f2552627ff638be9413ad4754ef581`, tested merge
+`b684654080d4f22cc1cf8d03e56cc523f4df3d57`, shared tree
+`179b7a51a4dd021dd62a42847c91b9575d76eb1a` received both independent 98/100
+pre-push grades. Native run41900102794 attempt1 passed Chrome126819901056 and
+Firefox126819901624, with independent complete-flow audits. This was Firefox's
+first actual execution; previous capacity failures remain unexecuted.
+
+Safari126819901608 passed capability, offline content/images, edits, reconnect
+and conflict-copy stages, then failed before any cache/localStorage/database
+mutation. At19:56:26.476Z unregister had returned true and registrations were
+empty, while the inert document still had a controller. PID7804 exited; the same
+profile restarted as PID11512. At19:56:34.873Z strict verification found the root
+registration and controller again. The final process exit was witnessed. This is
+not SPN-140's constructor failure; the Safari persistence mechanism is unproven.
+
+📦 [Immutable first failure, all native reports/images/logs and independent reviews](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/tree/f8e24b41b73eb9d4414597aba2c3396a931a9408/docs/review-assets/spn-141-native-388262cc)
+preserve artifact13359075911, ZIP SHA-256
+`0c0148ac6d286b3d5f5c01c55ff152054c6f61f458d5f557f125a05107e0b318`.
+Ordinary CI41900102989 and Storybook41900102783 were incomplete snapshots in
+that first archive. Their terminal attempt1 receipts are now preserved in
+[the later integration evidence](evidence/SPN-141-after143/README.md): CI was
+completed/cancelled and Storybook completed/success on exact388262cc. Ten CI
+workers and the browser aggregate were cancelled; Unit aggregate126833489868
+failed closed with `Incomplete coverage unit-tests: selected=true, result=cancelled`.
+That failed aggregate represents a cancelled selected worker, not a retained
+unit assertion failure; the raw aggregate log confirms the cause. This source
+never completed ordinary acceptance and receives no current-source credit.
+No old native pass validates this repair.
+
+The [Service Workers unregister and registration-clearing algorithms](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#unregister-algorithm)
+retain controlled clients after unregister and revisit clearing when the last
+client unloads or pending events settle. This motivates an explicit client-release
+boundary; it does not prove why the failed Safari run restored registration.
+The new choice supersedes immediate shutdown after unregistration above: once
+unregister succeeds, navigate every fixture-origin tab once to the inert route
+with a distinct query. A lost page-only marker proves a new document, and each
+tab must report complete loading, the inert marker, zero scripts and no controller.
+Account for all Safari window/tab positions or WebDriver handle membership;
+leave unrelated origins untouched. A same-document URL change cannot pass.
+Observe zero registrations and no controller once more before quitting, without
+deleting anything. Retain witnessed same-profile shutdown/restart and the unchanged
+strict post-restart storage precondition. A restored registration still fails
+before deletion. Null controllers do not independently prove every extended event
+finished, so the process and post-restart witnesses remain necessary.
+
+Reject another unregister, another deletion, fixed sleeps, deadline extensions
+and unchanged-source reruns. Safari retains its existing 2-second inventory
+observation within one 5-second native request; failed native requests propagate
+immediately. Each new browser observation uses the existing 28/30-second bound.
+No product behavior, routing exclusion, runner matrix or job budget changes.
+The complete outcome remains L: native lifecycle acceptance is retained here;
+SPN-140 constructor work and SPN-120's finite audit retain their separate scope.
+
+Operator gains evidence that the old controlled clients were actually released.
+Owner and Collaborator keep exact persisted-content and recovery assertions.
+Link guest access is unchanged; synthetic fixture isolation keeps this preparation
+away from user documents. All four favor observable release over guessing a delay.
+
+🧪 [Handoff local evidence, first failed fixture control and source hashes](evidence/SPN-141-handoff.json)
+records 46 passing actual serialized controls, full lint/dependency/format and
+focused types for all five changed roots/imports. The first controlled-client
+negative used an invalid mock controller without scriptURL; correcting the mock
+preserves the real controller contract. An initial compiler command named a
+nonexistent package; the corrected repository compiler passed. Neither failed
+attempt is omitted. Full hosted types/native acceptance remain pending.
+
+After complete-candidate commit and two new independent qualifying reviews,
+declare one repair synchronization of PR #258: all selected ordinary checks and
+one first-attempt Chrome/Safari/Firefox native workflow, unchanged assertions and
+budgets. Hypothesis: releasing every controlled client before normal shutdown
+establishes the missing lifecycle boundary. No further unchanged scenario or
+provisioning retry is included. Preserve any new first failure and assess it.
+

ci.prTitle: 🧽 SPN-141 Make native storage-loss preparation quiescent

metadata.gitDiff:
diff --git a/docs/implementation/SPN-141.md b/docs/implementation/SPN-141.md
index e1fddd8..0dc46cb 100644
--- a/docs/implementation/SPN-141.md
+++ b/docs/implementation/SPN-141.md
@@ -53,6 +53,351 @@ the post-loss assertions and every selected browser. Keep raw first failures and
 source/base/tested identities. Both independent exact-source grades precede push;
 mocks, unexecuted checks and retries cannot establish native acceptance.
 
+## 🧽 Leave active producers before deleting storage
+
+**2026-11-04, accepted implementation choice; agent judgment under the owner's
+request to continue SPN-120. Native acceptance remains pending.**
+
+The catalog effect in `web/offline/useOfflineDownloads.ts` explicitly calls
+`prepareShell` for retained downloads. That reaches the worker's `prepare`
+command and `fillRuntime` in `web/offline/runtimeCache.ts`, whose `caches.open`
+can create the shell cache. The original trace does not identify which invocation
+recreated it; this is a concrete concurrent producer, not proof of an OS defect.
+[The service-worker lifecycle](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-service-workers-20261029/#unregister-algorithm)
+also explains why successful unregistration alone is insufficient: existing
+controlled clients and pending events can retain the worker.
+
+Choose a fixture-owned, same-origin inert document, with no scripts and a
+`default-src 'none'` policy. Navigate there after positively proving two available
+copies; this unloads the application's refresh/registration producers. Unregister
+workers there, retaining the still-present controller in evidence. Witness the
+existing adapter's graceful browser/driver exit, then reopen exactly that document
+through the existing `launch` function, which verifies the same profile and version.
+Only then delete storage, requiring the expected document, zero scripts, zero
+registered workers and no controller before the first storage mutation. The fresh
+document cannot start an application or worker. This is preparation, not a retry
+of deletion or of a failed postcondition.
+
+Keep one deletion request, the 28-second operation report inside the 30-second
+driver bound, the existing launch/stop bounds and 25-minute job bound. The separate
+unregistration request has the same 28-second bound and performs no cache/database
+deletion. Its failure prevents restart/deletion; stop/start failures remain fatal
+and flow through existing owned cleanup. Exactly one extra witnessed browser exit
+and same-profile start is expected per native owner. The final storage postconditions
+and all post-loss application assertions are unchanged. Other IndexedDB names remain
+diagnostics; only the private account database is targeted. No product path changes.
+
+Reject deletion from the active catalog, repeating cache deletion, fixed settling
+delays and broader timeouts. Navigation alone cannot prove that a pending worker
+event stopped; the owned restart supplies the additional lifecycle boundary.
+No general process or automation framework is added. Complete scope remains **L**:
+shared native fixture/lifecycle integration, negative controls and three-browser
+acceptance, with Safari's independent constructor defect still owned by SPN-140.
+
+Operator receives explicit preparation and deletion stages with first causes.
+Owner and Collaborator keep exact retained/reconnected/conflict content and honest
+missing-copy proof. Link guest access is unchanged. All four personas favor the
+strict absence check over accepting a cache that may still be populated.
+
+## 🔎 Concrete test plan and publication checkpoint
+
+`scripts/ci/desktop-storage.test.ts` owns deterministic serialized-script controls:
+the inert-document requirement, registration/controller rejection before mutation,
+unregistration without deletion, re-registration, successful deletion followed by
+cache recreation, blocked/retained databases, pending/rejected operations and a
+crashed driver with no diagnostic second request. First focused execution: **25/25
+passed**, 323 ms including watchdog, peak 92,560 KiB, normal memory pressure.
+It does not prove browser process lifetimes or native acceptance.
+
+The existing Desktop offline workflow owns that integration. Before publishing,
+declare **one first-attempt workflow triggered by this candidate's PR opening**:
+Chrome and Firefox on macOS 26, Safari on macOS 15 Intel, unchanged owners and
+25-minute bounds. Expect the original exact content/images/reconnect/conflict
+checks, inert preparation and unregistration, a fourth same-profile launch/exit,
+strict empty-storage proof and both post-loss assertions for every owner. Safari
+must also pass the unchanged capability sentinel/identity/baseline checks. Preserve
+any first failure; no unchanged rerun or automatic renewal is part of this plan.
+
+All changed runtime/test files are under `scripts/ci/desktop-*.ts`, already selected
+by the native workflow. Ordinary unknown script paths conservatively select full
+CI; no routing, assertion, retry or applicability change is needed. Full constrained
+typecheck and lint, backlog/index/PR validation and two independent committed-source
+grades precede publication. Hosted ordinary gates and selected native evidence
+remain pending until observed on the exact source/tested identities.
+
+Local constrained typecheck was **resource-aborted**, not passed: the watchdog
+observed macOS pressure level 2 after 1,706 ms at 1,296,288 KiB. Subsequent
+format/focused-control/lint launches were refused at pressure 2. The first 25-test
+pass predates only a tighter asynchronous cache-recreation control and formatting;
+that refinement requires a fresh run when pressure is normal. Retain both results.
+
+## 🏁 Prepared landing bookkeeping
+
+Delete SPN-141's ticket, remove its dependency from SPN-120, append its completion
+counter and regenerate the index in this candidate. These are prepared landing
+changes; they do not declare pending native acceptance complete. SPN-140 and
+SPN-120 retain their own full obligations. Final run identities, measured results,
+both exact-source reviews and failure dispositions belong in the PR description
+or immutable maintained evidence before obsolete branches are removed.
+
+## 🔎 Independent review repair: restored background clients
+
+Both nonimplementing reviewers rejected candidate
+`14147960accca0927f0b61dfd4c66b7de98685ec`: A **94/100** (35/20/19/10/10),
+B **92/100** (31/23/18/10/10). Their shared P2 finding was concrete: the existing
+Safari adapter permits restored background tabs, so checking the selected inert
+document alone does not establish producer quiescence. No validation push occurred.
+
+Repair the same acceptance gap here. The owned adapter inventories every window/tab
+(Safari) or WebDriver window handle (Chrome/Firefox). Before unregistration, navigate
+other tabs on this exact fixture origin to the inert URL once; leave unrelated
+origins unchanged. Retain before/after URL inventories. After the witnessed restart,
+inventory again in read-only mode and reject any fixture-origin URL other than the
+inert document; do not navigate a newly restored producer and proceed. WebDriver
+also rejects a changed handle set during inventory. Empty/malformed inventories
+and a missing inert tab fail. Existing PID/start identity is checked before native
+inventory; this adds no authority over a browser outside the owned adapter.
+
+Safari waits for the one navigation's observable URL result within two seconds,
+inside a five-second command bound; a pending navigation is never repeated. An
+inventory failure remains fatal and enters existing teardown. The inert page's
+script/worker/controller checks and strict storage deletion still follow this
+whole-browser boundary. No new product feature or broader framework is needed;
+scope remains L. Both reviewers must revalidate the repaired committed head.
+
+Added negative controls cover a background producer after restart, missing/empty
+inventories, unrelated origins, and navigation that never settles. The actual
+serialized Safari inventory script is exercised, including once-only mutation of
+the other fixture tab. **33/33 controls passed**, 300 ms including watchdog, peak
+91,328 KiB. Full lint/dependency/format checks passed in 16,916 ms at peak 766,704 KiB,
+with normal pressure throughout. These results supersede the pending tightened
+control/lint attempts above without erasing their resource dispositions. Hosted
+whole-browser process/native behavior remains explicitly pending.
+
+The repaired source's constrained full typecheck was also resource-aborted:
+pressure level 2 after 3,251 ms, peak observed 1,360,048 KiB. No TypeScript success
+is claimed and no diagnostic was emitted before termination. Hosted Typecheck
+owns the remaining check; do not repeatedly load this Mac under pressure.
+
+During revalidation of `cef07957450cfaddc23014c1533131371b656a3b`, reviewer A
+identified a second fixture weakness: WebDriver handle order is not stable.
+Compare validated unique handle membership rather than ordered arrays, retaining
+rejection of new/missing/duplicate/malformed handles. Add the reordered-same-set
+positive control and changed-set negatives before final committed-source review.
+The [WebDriver specification](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#get-window-handles)
+permits arbitrary order. A scored this source 96/100 (35/23/18/10/10) with that
+finding still open; B independently scored it 98/100 (35/25/18/10/10). Neither
+score authorized pushing with A's unresolved defect. After the repair, **34/34
+controls passed** in 301 ms at 91,360 KiB; formatting and changed-file lint passed.
+Both final reviews must identify the new committed source.
+
+## 📦 First hosted source and prerequisite integration
+
+2026-11-04 — candidate `2f1c9304b15adfef833e53f12c4facff9ce14821`
+received independent pre-push grades A99/100 (35/25/19/10/10) and B98/100
+(35/25/18/10/10), with both findings above resolved. Tested merge
+`a554c611c96556176bcc6b2ba006ea421ee00943` and source share tree
+`faac771987098438ff4f9269ef27d20a1a2bb7e2` on main
+`5d8676ec280ac6d5cc9dcedb7e9cc09527b24806`. Agent review only.
+
+Native run41885019409 attempt1 passed Chrome job126767084103 and Safari
+job126767084191. Independent reviews accept each owner's same-profile lifecycle,
+original/pending content and image retention, exact reconnect, conflict copies,
+whole-browser inert inventories, uncontrolled deletion, empty storage witnesses
+and post-loss unavailable state. These actual runs each had one tab; deterministic
+controls own the background-tab negatives. Safari's earlier constructor failure
+is not erased, and SPN-140 remains separately required.
+
+Firefox job126767083588 never acquired a runner. Its zero runner ID, empty steps
+and hosted ARM64 capacity annotations support an infrastructure disposition,
+not a browser failure. A separately reviewed one-job provisioning allowance was
+[preserved before execution](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/tree/2bf0b3adba598239a953f87ae20ca485646f2fad/docs/review-assets/spn-141-native-2f1c9304/provisioning).
+Attempt2/job126779992912 also ended without a runner or any steps. Chrome/Safari
+entries carried into attempt2 retain their original execution timestamps; they
+were not run again. The allowance is exhausted; no further unchanged provisioning
